title: The psychology of spending, debt and budgeting, with Abigail Sussman, PhD

sentences.en: If you've bought anything in the last few years, you've probably encountered a new way of paying for your purchases.
sentences.zh: 如果你在过去几年里买过东西，你可能已经接触到了一种新的支付方式。

sentences.en: When you check out at the grocery store or hit Pay Now in your online shopping cart, you're asked,
sentences.zh: 当你在杂货店结账或在网购购物车中点击“立即支付”时，系统会问你：

sentences.en: do you want to pay in full today or split your purchase into four installments to be paid over time?
sentences.zh: 你是想今天全额支付，还是将购买金额分成四期分期付款？

sentences.en: The prevalence and popularity of these Buy Now, Pay Later services has surged in recent years.
sentences.zh: 近年来，这些“先买后付”服务的普及度和受欢迎程度激增。

sentences.en: One 2025 survey found that more than half of Americans had used a Buy Now, Pay Later service, such as Afterpay, Klarna, or Zip in the prior 12 months.
sentences.zh: 2025年的一项调查发现，超过半数的美国人在过去12个月内使用过Afterpay、Klarna或Zip等“先买后付”服务。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to explore the psychology of spending, budgeting, and debt, including the rise of Buy Now, Pay Later services.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨消费、预算和债务背后的心理学，包括“先买后付”服务的兴起。

sentences.en: How does the way we pay for a purchase affect our spending decisions?
sentences.zh: 我们的支付方式如何影响消费决策？

sentences.en: Why is it so easy to overspend?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们如此容易超支？

sentences.en: Why do people not pay off their credit card balances even when they have the cash?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们即使手头有现金，也不去偿还信用卡余额？

sentences.en: And how can we make better financial decisions in an increasingly complex and tempting financial landscape?
sentences.zh: 在一个日益复杂且充满诱惑的金融环境中，我们该如何做出更好的财务决策？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Abigail Sussman, the V.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是阿比盖尔·萨斯曼博士，她是

sentences.en: Duane Rath Professor of Marketing at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥大学布斯商学院的V.杜安·拉斯市场营销学教授。

sentences.en: She studies the psychological biases that lead people to make errors in budgeting, spending, borrowing, and investing.
sentences.zh: 她研究导致人们在预算、消费、借贷和投资方面犯错的心理偏差。

sentences.en: Her research investigates questions at the intersection of psychology, economics, and finance, with the aim of improving people's financial well-being.
sentences.zh: 她的研究调查了心理学、经济学和金融学交叉领域的问题，旨在改善人们的财务状况。

sentences.en: Her work has been featured in top academic journals, including the Journal of Consumer Research, the Journal of Experimental Psychology, and the Journal of Finance,
sentences.zh: 她的研究成果发表在《消费者研究期刊》、《实验心理学期刊》和《金融期刊》等顶级学术期刊上，

sentences.en: as well as popular media outlets, including National Public Radio, the New York Times, and the Wall Street Journal.
sentences.zh: 也出现在美国国家公共电台、《纽约时报》和《华尔街日报》等大众媒体上。

sentences.en: She recently spoke to APA's magazine Monitor on Psychology for an article about the psychology of debt and Buy Now, Pay Later loans.
sentences.zh: 她最近接受了美国心理学会杂志《心理学监测》的采访，讨论了关于债务心理学和“先买后付”贷款的文章。

sentences.en: Dr. Sussman, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 萨斯曼博士，感谢您今天参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I'm really happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: So I want to start by talking about what I mentioned a moment ago in the introduction, which is these Buy Now, Pay Later services that have spiked in popularity.
sentences.zh: 我想先从我刚才在介绍中提到的内容谈起，也就是那些人气飙升的“先买后付”服务。

sentences.en: What do we know about how they change people's spending behavior?
sentences.zh: 关于它们如何改变人们的消费行为，我们了解到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, so one of the things that we know is that they lead people to spend more.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们知道的一点是，它们会导致人们花更多的钱。

sentences.en: And we can think about what happens in terms of the underlying psychology here, which is that you go to make a purchase and you learn that instead of having to pay $100 today,
sentences.zh: 我们可以思考一下其背后的心理机制：当你去购物时，你发现与其今天支付100美元，

sentences.en: you only have to pay $25.
sentences.zh: 你只需要支付25美元。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, the purchase that seemed really expensive suddenly feels very affordable.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，原本看起来很贵的商品，瞬间变得非常实惠。

sentences.en: And if you don't really stop to think through what the implications are, you think, actually, maybe I can buy four different things for $25
sentences.zh: 如果你没有停下来仔细思考这意味着什么，你可能会想：或许我可以买四样不同的东西，每样25美元，

sentences.en: and spend the same $100 that I had intended to spend today for the single product.
sentences.zh: 花掉我原本打算今天为那一件商品支付的100美元。

sentences.en: And so as a result, it leads us to spend more without really feeling like we're doing so.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们在不知不觉中花了更多的钱。

sentences.en: Well, why does buying something with installment payments feel different from just putting it on a credit card?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么用分期付款买东西的感觉，和直接刷信用卡不一样呢？

sentences.en: You know, I think that one of the main characteristics that differentiates the Buy Now, Pay Later plans is the sticker price.
sentences.zh: 我认为，“先买后付”计划与信用卡的主要区别在于标价。

sentences.en: And so when you pay for something using a credit card, the cost that is displayed to you is the full cost of the product.
sentences.zh: 当你用信用卡支付时，显示给你的成本是产品的全额成本。

sentences.en: When you buy something using a Buy Now, Pay Later plan, what you're really seeing is the cost of the payment that you're making today.
sentences.zh: 而当你使用“先买后付”计划购买时，你真正看到的是你今天需要支付的那笔款项。

sentences.en: And so even if for the credit card, you might actually put something on your credit card and not pay any of it off for, let's say, a month,
sentences.zh: 即使对于信用卡，你可能刷了卡，比如一个月内都不还款，

sentences.en: but you're very aware of the fact that the amount that you're going to be paying is the full price and that in some sense you're borrowing the full price of the item
sentences.zh: 但你非常清楚你要支付的金额是全价，在某种意义上，你是在借贷商品的全部价格，

sentences.en: versus the Buy Now, Pay Later plan,
sentences.zh: 而相比之下，“先买后付”计划，

sentences.en: you're focused on the amount that you're paying today and it really dissociates the amount that you're going to be paying in the future periods.
sentences.zh: 你关注的是今天支付的金额，这实际上将你未来需要支付的金额与当前消费剥离了开来。

sentences.en: Stepping back for a minute, your research has looked more broadly at why we overspend and make less than optimal financial choices.
sentences.zh: 退一步说，您的研究更广泛地考察了我们为何会超支并做出次优的财务选择。

sentences.en: And one thing you've found is that we aren't very good at accounting for unexpected expenses in our budgets.
sentences.zh: 您发现的一点是，我们在预算中不太擅长考虑意外支出。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that work?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这项工作吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So I guess I would say why we maybe overspend relative to what we would expect to spend.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，为什么我们相对于预期支出而言可能会超支。

sentences.en: It's hard to say what's optimal in that in some cases we also are underspending, so we don't always give ourselves the pleasures that maybe would be beneficial.
sentences.zh: 很难说什么是“最优”，因为在某些情况下我们也在缩减开支，所以我们并不总是给自己提供可能是有益的享受。

sentences.en: So it sort of depends on who you are and what your financial situation is, what the optimal level is, but often we overspend relative to what we expect
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于你是谁以及你的财务状况如何，什么是最优水平，但我们往往相对于预期

sentences.en: or relative to what we would plan for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 或相对于我们为自己规划的支出而言，超支了。

sentences.en: And I think those cases we could really describe this sort of suboptimal.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这些情况下，我们可以将其描述为次优的。

sentences.en: And so a lot of this research started actually before I became a psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的很大一部分实际上是在我成为心理学家之前就开始的。

sentences.en: I was working in equity research and studied airlines.
sentences.zh: 当时我在做股票研究，研究航空公司。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that I noticed in that context
sentences.zh: 我在那个背景下注意到的一件事是，

sentences.en: was my job was basically to predict the financial statements of firms in future periods.
sentences.zh: 我的工作基本上是预测公司未来期间的财务报表。

sentences.en: And for airlines, if you were trying to predict what this airline was going to spend in the next period or the next quarter,
sentences.zh: 对于航空公司，如果你试图预测这家航空公司在下一期或下一季度将花费多少，

sentences.en: what you would do is you would try to think about what did they spend in the past quarter or over the past several quarters?
sentences.zh: 你会尝试思考它们在过去一个季度或过去几个季度花费了多少？

sentences.en: And then you would actually, you were specifically instructed from accounting rules to pull out these unusual expenses.
sentences.zh: 然后，根据会计准则，你会被明确指示剔除这些异常支出。

sentences.en: So if you were an airline, let's say that there was some sort of restructuring that happened or planes were grounded or there was a hurricane or a strike
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一家航空公司，假设发生了一些重组，或者飞机停飞，或者发生了飓风或罢工，

sentences.en: or any number of different things that were unusual, okay?
sentences.zh: 或者任何其他异常情况，明白吗？

sentences.en: So you were instructed as the financial analyst to pull those items out and report them separately.
sentences.zh: 作为财务分析师，你被指示将这些项目剔除并单独报告。

sentences.en: And so when you were making your predictions, the intent was to exclude those items from what you would expect would happen in the next period, okay?
sentences.zh: 因此，当你进行预测时，目的是将这些项目从你预期下一期会发生的事情中排除，明白吗？

sentences.en: And this always seemed very interesting to me because it seemed like, well, in real life, these events keep recurring.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说一直很有趣，因为看起来在现实生活中，这些事件会不断重演。

sentences.en: And even in the context of the airlines at that time, something kept recurring.
sentences.zh: 即使在当时航空公司的背景下，某些事情也在不断重演。

sentences.en: And like you wouldn't have a strike again the next period, but maybe there would be a hurricane the next period or something damaged the airline fleet or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 虽然你可能不会在下一期再次遭遇罢工，但下一期可能会有飓风，或者某些东西损坏了机队，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And that led me to investigate the same kind of prediction error in the context of consumers.
sentences.zh: 这促使我调查消费者背景下同样的预测错误。

sentences.en: And so what I've found in my research is that people are very bad at predicting the idea that something unusual will happen when they don't know what that's going to be.
sentences.zh: 我的研究发现，人们在不知道未来会发生什么的情况下，很难预测到会有异常事件发生。

sentences.en: And so maybe like I'm spending extra money this quarter because it's Halloween and I have Halloween decorations and candy and whatever else.
sentences.zh: 也许我这个季度多花了钱，因为是万圣节，我买了万圣节装饰品、糖果等等。

sentences.en: And then suddenly it's like, you know, now it's the next month and it's Thanksgiving, but Thanksgiving doesn't happen again in December.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，下个月是感恩节，但感恩节在十二月不会再发生一次。

sentences.en: In December, it's Christmas.
sentences.zh: 十二月是圣诞节。

sentences.en: And then in January, it's New Year's.
sentences.zh: 一月是新年。

sentences.en: And in February, it's Valentine's Day.
sentences.zh: 二月是情人节。

sentences.en: And so each one of these times it's like, well, no, Valentine's Day is not happening again in March, right?
sentences.zh: 所以每一次都像是：好吧，情人节不会在三月再发生一次，对吧？

sentences.en: So and each time you're right that that particular expense is not going to recur.
sentences.zh: 所以你说的没错，那笔特定的支出不会重演。

sentences.en: And so I think that there's something around the psychology of it's very easy to think about what is the baseline set of expenses that we have.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中涉及心理学问题，即我们很容易想到我们的基准支出是多少。

sentences.en: So am I going to predict my grocery bills?
sentences.zh: 我会预测我的杂货账单吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like that's going to be sort of easy to predict my, you know, the cost of my mortgage or my rent.
sentences.zh: 这很容易预测，比如我的抵押贷款或房租成本。

sentences.en: Like, yes, I'm going to do that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会这样做。

sentences.en: And the cost of like, you know, usually I go out to dinner, you know, three times a month and I'm going to plan for that, too.
sentences.zh: 还有比如，我通常一个月出去吃三次饭，我也会为此做计划。

sentences.en: So that stuff is sort of stable and it factors very much into our predictions.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西是稳定的，非常符合我们的预测。

sentences.en: But what doesn't factor into these predictions are these outlier expenses.
sentences.zh: 但这些异常支出并没有被纳入预测。

sentences.en: And in some sense, as I think evidenced by this example from financial analysts, maybe they shouldn't because that particular expense isn't going to recur.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，正如财务分析师的例子所证明的那样，也许它们不应该被纳入，因为那笔特定的支出不会重演。

sentences.en: But in practice, what happens is that when you think about this category of unusual expenses, there's likely to be something that will fill that spot.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，当你想到这类异常支出时，很可能会有其他事情填补这个空缺。

sentences.en: And so it's really good to leave a placeholder to say, here's the thing that I'm not going to expect.
sentences.zh: 所以最好留一个占位符，说：这是我没预料到的事情。

sentences.en: We're going to leave a buffer for that.
sentences.zh: 我们要为此留出缓冲。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And do people tend to do that or is that just impossible?
sentences.zh: 人们倾向于这样做吗？还是说这根本不可能？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there were rules about you should have how many months of expenses in a rainy day fund just in case, one of those just in case things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，有一些规则建议你应该在应急基金中存够几个月的开支，以防万一，就是那种“以防万一”的事情。

sentences.en: Why is that such a problem for us?
sentences.zh: 为什么这对我们来说是个难题？

sentences.en: So I guess there are two different things.
sentences.zh: 我想这有两件不同的事情。

sentences.en: One is like you can have money that's set aside for a rainy day fund.
sentences.zh: 一是你可以有留作应急基金的钱。

sentences.en: But the question is, should you be tapping into that or should you actually plan on having that be part of your budget?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，你应该动用那笔钱，还是应该真正计划将其作为预算的一部分？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like you shouldn't you should have that as part of your rainy day fund.
sentences.zh: 你应该把它作为应急基金的一部分。

sentences.en: That's a separate question.
sentences.zh: 那是另一个问题。

sentences.en: And some of us are able to set aside that money and some of us aren't.
sentences.zh: 我们有些人能够存下那笔钱，而有些人则不能。

sentences.en: But the question is, on a monthly basis, why do we need to tap into the rainy day fund?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，在每个月的基础上，为什么我们需要动用应急基金？

sentences.en: Why can't we just plan for that in our budget?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能在预算中为此做好计划？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, why can't we anticipate these expenses?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能预见这些支出？

sentences.en: And what we find.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，

sentences.en: And so this is in research led by Chuck Howard in terms of this expense, the sort of prediction
sentences.zh: 这是由查克·霍华德领导的研究，关于这种支出，这种预测

sentences.en: error is that you can ask people basically repeatedly, how much did you spend last week?
sentences.zh: 错误在于，你可以反复问人们：你上周花了多少钱？

sentences.en: They'll say one hundred dollars.
sentences.zh: 他们会说100美元。

sentences.en: How much do you think you're going to spend next week?
sentences.zh: 你觉得下周你会花多少钱？

sentences.en: Eighty dollars.
sentences.zh: 80美元。

sentences.en: OK, a week later, how much did you spend last week?
sentences.zh: 好的，一周后，你上周花了多少钱？

sentences.en: A hundred dollars.
How much are you going to spend next week?
sentences.zh: 你下周打算花多少钱？

sentences.en: Eighty dollars.
sentences.zh: 80美元。

sentences.en: And people actually will just keep doing this over and over again.
sentences.zh: 人们实际上会一遍又一遍地这样做。

sentences.en: And what happens is that people essentially are predicting their modal spending and they're failing to anticipate any of these sorts of outlier expenses.
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，人们本质上是在预测他们的典型支出，而未能预见到任何此类异常支出。

sentences.en: Now, if you get people to stop and reflect on what do you think is going to be different next week and just to pause and think through this, they are able to identify what those
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你让人们停下来反思一下你认为下周会有什么不同，并暂停思考一下，他们是能够识别出这些

sentences.en: differences are likely to be.
sentences.zh: 差异可能是什么的。

sentences.en: But at baseline, it's not what what comes naturally to people.
sentences.zh: 但在基准情况下，这不是人们自然而然会想到的。

sentences.en: Instead, they're just going to think about what were the things that I spent money on last month?
sentences.zh: 相反，他们只会考虑上个月我把钱花在什么地方了？

sentences.en: Which of those are going to recur and sort of only project the ones that are going to recur going forward?
sentences.zh: 其中哪些会重演，并只把那些会重演的项目投射到未来。

sentences.en: And that's where you get this gap.
sentences.zh: 这就是差距产生的地方。

sentences.en: And one of the other consequences of focusing on this is that people tend to actually spend more on these one off expenses than they might otherwise because they think of them as
sentences.zh: 关注这一点的另一个后果是，人们实际上往往会在这些一次性支出上花更多的钱，因为他们认为这些支出是

sentences.en: exceptional.
sentences.zh: 例外的。

sentences.en: And so if I think, you know, this this particular kind of expense, it's like I'm buying a birthday present, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我想，你知道，这种特定的支出，比如我正在买一份生日礼物，

sentences.en: For example, this only happens once a year, well, then I can afford to spend more on it.
sentences.zh: 例如，这每年只发生一次，那么我就可以负担得起多花点钱。

sentences.en: And so it also licenses you again, because I'm not thinking about it as a recurring expense.
sentences.zh: 所以它也给了你一种许可，因为我没有把它当作经常性支出。

sentences.en: And so the cost is only one higher price rather than, you know, 15 higher prices, if you think about the fact that similar kinds of expenses occur 15 times throughout the year.
sentences.zh: 所以成本只是一个较高的价格，而不是，你知道，15个较高的价格，如果你考虑到类似的支出在一年中会发生15次的话。

sentences.en: So how do stores and retailers take advantage of the psychological biases we experience when they're trying to sell us products?
sentences.zh: 那么商店和零售商在试图向我们推销产品时，是如何利用我们经历的心理偏差的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I think that there that's a very broad question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个非常广泛的问题。

sentences.en: And I think there are many different things that stores do in terms of one is bringing this
sentences.zh: 我认为商店做了很多不同的事情，其中之一就是把这个

sentences.en: idea back to the buy now pay later plans, which is really how do you think about the costs and the benefits and the timing of various costs and benefits?
sentences.zh: 想法带回到“先买后付”计划上，这实际上就是你如何思考各种成本和收益的成本、收益以及时间安排？

sentences.en: And so to the extent that you can focus people on the benefits that they'll get today and the costs that will come later.

sentences.en: And so here companies can be very good at helping combine or bundle products together and advertise
sentences.zh: 在这里，公司非常擅长帮助组合或捆绑产品，并宣传

sentences.en: what might actually be something that's a superfluous product, but that feels like, well, if I'm buying this, I'll actually probably save money over time by buying this additional

sentences.en: compliment.

sentences.en: In addition to just being so good at predicting things that you might want and suddenly feel like you actually need to have them.
sentences.zh: 除了非常擅长预测你可能想要的东西，并让你突然觉得你实际上需要拥有它们之外。

sentences.en: So I think firms have gotten very good at predicting their customers' needs and wants and desires and increasingly sort of throwing in more tempting options together.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为公司已经非常擅长预测客户的需求、愿望和渴望，并越来越多地将更多诱人的选项组合在一起。

sentences.en: And of course, AI keeps pushing things at us, whether we want them or not.
sentences.zh: 当然，人工智能不断地向我们推送东西，不管我们是否想要。

sentences.en: So one day you go and you look at a pair of shoes and now for the next three weeks, all you see in your feed is shoes, shoes, shoes.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天你去看了双鞋，接下来的三周里，你的信息流里全是鞋子、鞋子、鞋子。

sentences.en: And they're like, I guess I did want those.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我想我确实想要那些。

sentences.en: Or you left this in your card, you know, all of those kinds of little tips and tricks.
sentences.zh: 或者你把这个留在购物车里，你知道，所有这些小技巧。

sentences.en: You looked at this on eBay.
sentences.zh: 你在eBay上看了这个。

sentences.en: It's still for sale.
sentences.zh: 它还在卖。

sentences.en: You know, come back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，回来吧。

sentences.zh: 价格刚刚降了100美元。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 而且我认为“价格刚刚降了”是另一个有趣的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: Like how do firms think about advertising discounts?
sentences.zh: 公司如何考虑宣传折扣？

sentences.en: How do firms take advantage of sort of a limited time opportunity, right?
sentences.zh: 公司如何利用某种限时机会，对吧？

sentences.en: So I think from a scarcity perspective, you don't want to miss out on an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为从稀缺性的角度来看，你不想错过机会。

sentences.en: And that opportunity can be a discount as well.
sentences.zh: 而那个机会也可以是一个折扣。

sentences.en: And that's something that people get a lot of value from feeling like they've gotten a deal.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得捡到了便宜，这本身就能带来很大的价值感。

sentences.en: And that's another place where we see stores taking, I mean, being very aware of what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们看到商家非常清楚自己在做什么的另一个方面。

sentences.en: The more you spend, the more you save.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: When we return, I'll talk with Dr. Sussman about keeping up with the Joneses and how people think differently about wealth and debt when they're comparing their own spending with
sentences.zh: 回来后，我将与萨斯曼博士探讨“攀比心理”，以及人们在将自己的消费与邻居的消费进行比较时，对财富和债务的看法有何不同。

sentences.en: their neighbor's spending.
sentences.zh: 邻居的消费。

sentences.en: Now, you've also studied how people think differently about wealth and debt when they're comparing their own spending to their neighbor's spending.
sentences.zh: 现在，您也研究过人们在将自己的消费与邻居的消费进行比较时，对财富和债务的看法有何不同。

sentences.en: How does social comparisons shape our spending and saving behaviors?
sentences.zh: 社会比较是如何塑造我们的消费和储蓄行为的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So one of the things I think that was the insight of this paper that you're mentioning with
sentences.zh: 我认为您提到的这篇与拉斐尔·巴蒂斯塔和詹妮弗·特鲁布拉德合著的论文，其洞见之一在于，当我们思考社会比较时，多年来已经有大量关于“炫耀性消费”的研究，即我们观察他人的购买行为并据此进行推断。
zh_words: 詹妮弗·特鲁布拉德合著

sentences.en: Raphael Batista and Jennifer Trueblood, one of the insights there is basically that when we think about social comparison, there's been a lot of work for many, many, many, many
sentences.zh: 多年来，人们一直在研究炫耀性消费，即我们观察他人的购买行为并据此进行推断。

sentences.en: years on conspicuous consumption, thinking about we observe what other people are purchasing and we draw inferences from that.
sentences.zh: 多年来，人们一直在研究炫耀性消费，即我们观察他人的购买行为并据此进行推断。

sentences.en: And similarly, we want to consume fancy cars, fancy clothing, right, that we know other people
sentences.zh: 同样，我们想要消费名车、名牌服装，对吧，因为我们知道别人会看到，并且会因为我们消费了这些东西而对我们评价更高。

sentences.en: are going to look at and they're going to think more highly of us, for example, for consuming those things.
sentences.zh: 我们知道别人会看到，并且会因为我们消费了这些东西而对我们评价更高。

sentences.en: One of the things that is less visible and generally actually not talked about at all is not the consumption side of things, but the saving and debt side, right?
sentences.zh: 有一点不太显眼，而且通常根本没人谈论，那就是储蓄和债务方面，而不是消费方面，对吧？

sentences.en: And so we really don't know how much debt somebody has.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道某人背负了多少债务。

sentences.en: We don't know how much money somebody has in their savings account.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道某人的储蓄账户里有多少钱。

sentences.en: And I think that to some degree, this puts us as a society at a huge disadvantage because
sentences.zh: 我认为在某种程度上，这让我们整个社会处于巨大的劣势，因为

sentences.en: you end up at this keeping up with the Joneses for, in some sense, the things that are maybe the least important aspects of consumption, whereas the things that actually provide us
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你最终陷入了这种“攀比”之中，而攀比的对象可能恰恰是消费中最不重要的方面，然而那些真正能为我们提供财务稳定感和财务舒适感的东西——这些非常重要的东西——却无法传递任何身份地位的信号。

sentences.en: with financial stability and feelings of financial comfort, which are really important, are not going to be sending any sort of signal of status.
sentences.zh: 真正能为我们提供财务稳定感和财务舒适感的东西——这些非常重要的东西——却无法传递任何身份地位的信号。

sentences.en: And so what ends up happening is that we evaluate people based on their spending.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们根据人们的消费来评价他们。

sentences.en: And I think that the fact that if we look at what somebody else has spent, we don't have visibility into the debt that they took on, let's say, in our own spending, we're very
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果我们只看别人花了多少钱，却看不到他们背负的债务，那么在审视我们自己的消费时，我们对债务是非常敏感的。

sentences.en: aware of the debt.
sentences.zh: 对债务是非常敏感的。

sentences.en: And so when we think about sort of evaluating how wealthy does this make me feel, I'm going
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们考虑评估这让我感觉有多富有的时候，我会非常在意为了进行这次特定购买我背负了多少债务，而不是去评估别人。

sentences.en: to be very sensitive to how much debt I took on in order to make this particular purchase and not evaluating somebody else.
sentences.zh: 而不是去评估别人。

sentences.en: And so this has the potential to actually really aggravate and exacerbate this conspicuous consumption cycle.
sentences.zh: 因此，这有可能真正加剧并恶化这种炫耀性消费的循环。

sentences.en: Between inflation and job instability, a lot of people are feeling financially stressed right now.
sentences.zh: 在通货膨胀和工作不稳定的双重压力下，很多人现在感到财务压力很大。

sentences.en: How do stress and economic uncertainty change the way that people make spending decisions?
sentences.zh: 压力和经济不确定性是如何改变人们的消费决策方式的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is, I think, a really important question right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: And I think that in many cases, it makes people more myopic.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，这会让人们变得更加短视。

sentences.en: And so I'm going to be more focused on what is my budget this month.
sentences.zh: 我会更关注我这个月的预算是多少。

sentences.en: And I'm going to be really focused on trying to stay within my means for, let's say, I would set specific budget categories.
sentences.zh: 我会非常专注于量入为出，比如，我会设定具体的预算类别。

sentences.en: And on a day-to-day basis, make sure that I'm spending less.
sentences.zh: 并且在日常生活中，确保我的支出更少。

sentences.en: But I'm more likely to lose sight of the bigger picture financial goals.
sentences.zh: 但我更容易忽略长期的财务目标。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that we find is that people with lower incomes and more financial instability actually find budgeting also less pleasant and are less likely to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，收入较低且财务状况不稳定的人，实际上觉得做预算更不愉快，也更不容易去做预算。

sentences.en: But conditional on engaging in budgeting, people are checking their budgets more, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果真的开始做预算，人们反而会更频繁地查看预算，对吧？

sentences.en: So it becomes more of an exercise of making ends meet rather than thinking about striving
sentences.zh: 所以这更多变成了一种维持生计的练习，而不是去思考如何争取更好的生活，或者思考更长期的财务目标，我认为这只是由约束和限制自然而然产生的结果。

sentences.en: for something better or thinking about longer-term financial goals, which is just one of the, I think, just something that falls out naturally from the constraints and limitations.
sentences.zh: 我认为这只是由约束和限制自然而然产生的结果。

sentences.en: Another related piece of work looks at the effect of actually losing one's job on financial risk-taking.
sentences.zh: 另一项相关研究着眼于失业对财务风险承担的影响。

sentences.en: And in this work with Sam Hirschman and Jennifer Trueblood, we find that actually after losing
sentences.zh: 在与萨姆·赫什曼和詹妮弗·特鲁布拉德合作的这项研究中，我们发现，失业后，人们的总支出确实减少了，但他们在赌博或其他风险财务行为上的支出，相对于其他支出而言，减少得较少。

sentences.en: one's job, people spend less overall, but actually the amount that they spend on something like
sentences.zh: 实际上，失业后，人们的总支出确实减少了，但他们在赌博或其他风险财务行为上的支出，相对于其他支出而言，减少得较少。

sentences.en: gambling or other kinds of risky financial behaviors decreases relatively less than other spending.
sentences.zh: 实际上，失业后，人们的总支出确实减少了，但他们在赌博或其他风险财务行为上的支出，相对于其他支出而言，减少得较少。

sentences.en: And so what this suggests is that people really are hoping to make up for the amount that they've lost in these kinds of financial shock kinds of experiences.
sentences.zh: 这表明，人们确实希望在这些财务冲击经历中弥补他们所损失的金额。

sentences.en: So overall spending less, but still trying to remain in some sense like optimistic around this risk-taking behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说支出减少了，但仍然试图在某种程度上对这种风险行为保持乐观。

sentences.en: Do you have advice for people who would like to do a better job of sticking to their budget?
sentences.zh: 对于那些想要更好地坚持预算的人，您有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: Are there, is there anything in your research that suggests strategies that we can use in our everyday lives?
sentences.zh: 您的研究中是否有任何建议可以应用到我们的日常生活中？

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: So I think there are a couple of, a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几点建议。

sentences.en: So one is trying to set a realistic budget in the first place.
sentences.zh: 首先是尽量设定一个现实的预算。

sentences.en: I think that's going to be key.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是关键。

sentences.en: And so that includes things like either leaving a buffer for unusual kinds of expenses or one-off expenses.
sentences.zh: 这包括为不寻常的开支或一次性开支留出缓冲空间。

sentences.en: And you could think about rather than going back and thinking on a category by category basis,
sentences.zh: 你可以考虑不要回头去按类别思考，

sentences.en: how much have I spent in each month, let's say, look at your aggregate spending and try to make sure that your budget matches the aggregate level of spending rather than summing
sentences.zh: 比如每个月花了多少钱，而是看看你的总支出，并尽量确保你的预算与总支出水平相匹配，而不是从底层按类别累加，如果这说得通的话，可以通过增加每个类别的金额或添加一个单独的储备金来实现。

sentences.en: up from the bottom by category, if that makes sense, either by increasing the amount in each category or adding a separate bucket.
sentences.zh: 如果这说得通的话，可以通过增加每个类别的金额或添加一个单独的储备金来实现。

sentences.en: Another thing is around this impulsivity and sort of buying based on the pair of shoes that was shown to you at each different website that you went to, right?
sentences.zh: 另一件事是关于这种冲动性，以及基于你在每个不同网站上看到的鞋子而进行的购买，对吧？

sentences.en: And so one of the things that's happened, I think, a lot is around just automating the purchasing process and reducing frictions for spending.
sentences.zh: 我认为发生了很多变化的一点是，消费过程的自动化和消费摩擦的减少。

sentences.en: And so if you, for me, let's say, like, right, if I go online to any store, all of a sudden
sentences.zh: 所以如果你，对我来说，比如，对吧，如果我上网去任何商店，突然间

sentences.en: the internet has my credit card information, like my computer has my information stored in five different ways.
sentences.zh: 互联网就有了我的信用卡信息，就像我的电脑以五种不同的方式存储了我的信息一样。

sentences.en: And it used to be like you had to, well, it used to be you had to take out cash from your wallet and you had to be in a store to make a payment.
sentences.zh: 过去你必须，嗯，过去你必须从钱包里拿出钱，而且必须在店里才能付款。

sentences.en: You thought a lot about what that payment was going to be right before you made it.
sentences.zh: 在付款之前，你会仔细考虑那笔钱是多少。

sentences.en: It was psychologically costly in addition to the dollar cost to separate with that money.
sentences.zh: 除了金钱成本之外，放弃那笔钱在心理上也是有代价的。

sentences.en: And now I don't even need to take out my credit card to make a payment.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我甚至不需要拿出信用卡就能付款。

sentences.en: I just have to keep sort of clicking through and everything is automatically filled in for me.
sentences.zh: 我只需要不断点击，一切都会自动为我填好。

sentences.en: And so to the extent that we can reintroduce frictions into our spending, this is something that's helpful.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们能在消费中重新引入摩擦，这会有所帮助。

sentences.en: And so making rules for yourself could be, I'm only going to buy in person, would be one kind of rule.
sentences.zh: 所以给自己定规矩，比如“我只在实体店购买”，这是一种规矩。

sentences.en: That comes with other challenges, which is like now you're at the store and now you're tempted by all of the different things in the store.
sentences.zh: 但这会带来其他挑战，比如你现在在店里，又会被店里各种各样的东西诱惑。

sentences.en: So sort of going with a more concrete plan in that case.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况下需要一个更具体的计划。

sentences.en: But I think just removing your credit card online, you know, taking it down from Google
sentences.zh: 但我认为，只要在网上删除你的信用卡信息，你知道，从谷歌支付和苹果支付中移除，这些事情就会让我们停下来反思。

sentences.en: Pay and Apple Pay, these kinds of things will just lead us to pause and reflect.
sentences.zh: 这些事情就会让我们停下来反思。

sentences.en: And we can still buy all of the things that we want to buy.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然可以购买我们想要的所有东西。

sentences.en: But really making sure that we've thought through these decisions, I think, is going to be one valuable one valuable component.
sentences.zh: 但确保我们已经深思熟虑过这些决定，我认为这将是一个有价值的组成部分。

sentences.en: And then the other is to try to be thoughtful about when we're spending.
sentences.zh: 另一个建议是尽量在消费时保持理性。

sentences.en: So setting aside specific times to be making purchases as opposed to either being online
sentences.zh: 设定特定的时间进行购物，而不是在上网时，

sentences.en: and sort of shopping out of, you know, different sorts of emotions or boredom or going to the supermarket even.
sentences.zh: 出于各种情绪或无聊而购物，甚至去超市也是如此。

sentences.en: And you can go to the supermarket when you're starving or you can go to the supermarket when you've come with a plan.
sentences.zh: 你可以在饿的时候去超市，也可以在有计划的时候去超市。

sentences.en: And if you go when you're starving, like probably you'll leave with a lot of Kit Kats and not necessarily the food that you needed.
sentences.zh: 如果你在饿的时候去，很可能会买一大堆奇巧巧克力，而不是你真正需要的食物。

sentences.en: And so going right.
sentences.zh: 所以去的时候，对。

sentences.en: And so being thoughtful, we sometimes think about this as as spending in a cold state, like when your emotions are low and you're not in sort of the heat of the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以要保持理性，我们有时认为这是一种“冷静状态”下的消费，即当你的情绪低落，不在那种冲动时刻的时候。

sentences.en: So we can think about that from a hunger perspective would be the analog for a grocery store.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以从饥饿的角度来思考这个问题，这相当于去杂货店的情况。

sentences.en: But you can think about this from other perspectives as well, depending on what the kind of purchase
sentences.zh: 但你也可以从其他角度来思考，取决于购买的类型，

sentences.en: is, but trying to sort of take the emotion out of the spending is another way to think about restraining our spending and staying within our budgets.
sentences.zh: 但尝试将情绪从消费中剥离出来，是另一种控制消费并保持在预算内的方法。

sentences.en: There seem to be a lot of apps out there these days that promise that they're going to help you get your financial life in order.
sentences.zh: 现在市面上似乎有很多应用程序承诺能帮你理清财务生活。

sentences.en: And, you know, I get all these ads for I'm not going to name it because they're not a sponsor,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我收到了所有这些广告，我不会点名，因为它们不是赞助商，

sentences.en: but there's a particular particular app that that that tells you, oh, you know, you've
sentences.zh: 但有一个特定的应用程序，它告诉你，哦，你知道，你

sentences.en: got four subscriptions to Netflix and you haven't watched Hulu in six months and and I'll cancel these things for you.
sentences.zh: 订阅了四个Netflix账号，而且你已经六个月没看Hulu了，我可以帮你取消这些订阅。

sentences.en: Do those apps really work for people or are we that are we that sad that we don't know how much we're we're subscribing to at this point?
sentences.zh: 这些应用程序真的对人们有用吗？还是说我们已经悲哀到连自己订阅了多少东西都不知道了？

sentences.en: We we need something else, something external to tell us.
sentences.zh: 我们需要其他东西，一些外部的东西来告诉我们。

sentences.en: I think that the topic of subscriptions is actually a big problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为订阅这个话题实际上是一个大问题。

sentences.en: People do not unsubscribe.
sentences.zh: 人们确实不会取消订阅。

sentences.en: So I actually think a lot of people have subscriptions that they are not paying attention to, that they're not aware of, that are automatically renewing.
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上认为很多人都有他们没有注意到的、不知道的、正在自动续订的订阅。

sentences.en: It's incredibly difficult.
sentences.zh: 这极其困难。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know, incredibly difficult, but oftentimes, right, signing up for something is very easy and you frequently will click a button that says auto renew or you won't be
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道，极其困难，但通常情况下，对吧，注册某样东西非常容易，而且你经常会点击一个写着“自动续订”的按钮，或者除非你同意自动续订，否则你就不被允许注册。

sentences.en: allowed to sign up unless you agree to auto renewal.
sentences.zh: 否则你就不被允许注册。

sentences.en: So I actually think the topic of apps is sort of it depends on what the app is and how helpful it could be.
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上认为应用程序这个话题，取决于应用程序是什么，以及它能有多大帮助。

sentences.en: Like, surely there there are apps out there that can be helpful for managing your finances.
sentences.zh: 比如，市面上肯定有一些应用程序对管理财务很有帮助。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that apps do is they also select on people who care and are focused on it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，应用程序所做的事情之一，也是筛选出那些关心并专注于此的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They bring your attention to these issues, which I think, again, can be very valuable.
sentences.zh: 它们让你关注这些问题，我认为这再次证明是非常有价值的。

sentences.en: I think for many people, it's easy to it's easy to lose track of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为对许多人来说，很容易忽略这些问题。

sentences.en: And companies are not always reminding you before that payment comes due, right?
sentences.zh: 而且公司并不总是在付款到期前提醒你，对吧？

sentences.en: Why would they?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要提醒？

sentences.en: They want your money.
sentences.zh: 他们想要你的钱。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: You've also looked at how people think about the tradeoff between savings and debt, especially something that's called co-holding.
sentences.zh: 您还研究过人们如何看待储蓄和债务之间的权衡，特别是所谓的“共同持有”。

sentences.en: I think I mentioned in the intro when people have credit card debt, but they also have money in savings and they could pay off that debt.
sentences.zh: 我想我在开场白中提到过，当人们有信用卡债务时，他们也有储蓄，他们本可以还清债务。

sentences.en: Does this ever make financial sense?
sentences.zh: 这在财务上真的合理吗？

sentences.en: And if not, why is it so common?
sentences.zh: 如果不是，为什么它如此普遍？

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So this is something that's quite common behavior.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常普遍的行为。

sentences.en: And there are cases where it could make financial sense.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，它在财务上可能是合理的。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you're worried that you won't have access to liquidity from your credit
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你担心未来无法从信用卡中获得流动性，

sentences.en: card in the future, then maybe you need that sort of savings buffer because that's the only way that you'll have cash to pay bills.
sentences.zh: 那么也许你需要那种储蓄缓冲，因为那是你支付账单的唯一现金来源。

sentences.en: That's the sort of thing that could make financial sense.
sentences.zh: 那确实可能在财务上说得通。

sentences.en: I think for many people who are engaging in co-holding, that's not the case, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为对于许多进行“共同持有”的人来说，情况并非如此，对吧？

sentences.en: If they would have, if you paid down your credit card bill this month, you could continue to borrow on credit the next month, for example.
sentences.zh: 如果你这个月还清了信用卡账单，下个月你仍然可以继续借贷，例如。

sentences.en: And I think there's also a question with co-holding of sort of how much money do you have in cash and how much money should you have in cash from a comfort or savings perspective?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为关于“共同持有”，还有一个问题是，从舒适度或储蓄的角度来看，你应该拥有多少现金？

sentences.en: So I think that there is definitely complexity there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这绝对存在复杂性。

sentences.en: But I think that a lot of what happens with co-holding, and there have been many different
sentences.zh: 但我认为“共同持有”中发生了很多事情，并且在经济学文献中已经提出了许多不同的解释，

sentences.en: explanations proposed, largely within the economics literature, I think that there's also something psychological going on where we feel responsible for having money and savings.
sentences.zh: 我认为也存在心理因素，我们觉得有责任在储蓄中存钱。

sentences.en: And we're able to, because of mental accounting, we mentally segregate savings and debt.
sentences.zh: 而且由于心理账户的存在，我们能够将储蓄和债务在心理上隔离开来。

sentences.en: So we don't think of it as having one pool of money, and that money is basically right, our savings minus our debt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会把它看作是一个资金池，而那个资金池基本上就是，对吧，我们的储蓄减去债务。

sentences.en: Instead, we think of it as two distinct pools.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们把它看作两个不同的池子。

sentences.en: And so our savings is on the right, our debt is on the left.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的储蓄在右边，债务在左边。

sentences.en: And to the extent that you think about these two things as distinct pools, well, what do people who are financially secure have?
sentences.zh: 如果你把这两者看作不同的池子，那么财务状况良好的人拥有什么？

sentences.en: They have money and savings.
sentences.zh: 他们有储蓄。

sentences.en: And so if I want to feel responsible, I'm going to have money and savings too.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我想让自己感觉负责任，我也会有储蓄。

sentences.en: And so this is something that I've worked on with Rourke O'Brien, looking at what happens
sentences.zh: 这是我和罗克·奥布莱恩合作研究的课题，观察当你储蓄中的钱被指定用于不同目的时会发生什么。

sentences.en: when the amount of the money that you have in savings is designated for different purposes.
sentences.zh: 观察当你储蓄中的钱被指定用于不同目的时会发生什么。

sentences.en: So if you think about this money that I've set aside in savings for something really responsible, so for my kids' education, for example, I'm not going to touch that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你认为我存下的这笔钱是为了非常负责任的事情，比如为了我孩子的教育，我是不会动它的。

sentences.en: And if some expense comes along, I'm going to instead borrow on my credit card, because of course, I'm not touching money that I've set aside for my kid or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 如果出现了一些开支，我会选择刷信用卡，因为当然，我不会动我为孩子存下的钱，或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: If I have money set aside for my vacation, I'll be more likely to draw that down.
sentences.zh: 如果我为度假存了钱，我更有可能动用那笔钱。

sentences.en: And so I do think people are able to segregate and say, like, yeah, it's bad that I have money in debt, but it's really important that I have money in savings.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为人们能够进行隔离，并说，是的，我有债务很糟糕，但拥有储蓄非常重要。

sentences.en: And what do these two things even have to do with each other?
sentences.zh: 这两者之间有什么关系呢？

sentences.en: And so more recently, in work led by Rafael Batista, again, we've done some research where
sentences.zh: 最近，在拉斐尔·巴蒂斯塔领导的研究中，我们再次进行了一些研究，

sentences.en: we've worked with a large bank in Australia, and we've partnered with them to actually run experiments where we're able to send people banking app notifications telling them that
sentences.zh: 我们与澳大利亚的一家大型银行合作，开展了实验，我们能够向人们发送银行应用程序通知，告诉他们

sentences.en: they have money in both savings and debt, and basically that this is a costly for them to do, that their credit card debt is being charged a high 15% interest, let's say, versus
sentences.zh: 他们同时有储蓄和债务，基本上这让他们付出了代价，他们的信用卡债务被收取了15%的高额利息，比如说，而他们的储蓄账户只获得1%的利息。

sentences.en: 1% interest that they're getting on their savings accounts.
sentences.zh: 而他们的储蓄账户只获得1%的利息。

sentences.en: And so sending these sorts of in-app notifications.
sentences.zh: 所以发送这些应用内通知。

sentences.en: And what we find is that it actually has minimal effect on behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们发现它对行为的影响实际上微乎其微。

sentences.en: So it doesn't seem like most people are doing this sort of by accident, but instead, it's quite deliberate.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人似乎并不是偶然这样做的，相反，这是相当深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: And so in more recent work, we're also looking into the idea that one of the things that we've
sentences.zh: 在最近的研究中，我们也在研究一个想法，即我们

sentences.en: noticed in terms of digging into transaction data around these customers is that the customers
sentences.zh: 在深入挖掘这些客户的交易数据时注意到的一件事是，那些

sentences.en: that tend to be co-holding tend also to be using their debit cards more for transactions.
sentences.zh: 倾向于“共同持有”的客户，在交易中也倾向于更多地使用借记卡。

sentences.en: And so this suggests that an additional factor beyond what I've already been talking about is
sentences.zh: 这表明，除了我之前提到的因素之外，还有一个额外因素，

sentences.en: that for people who want to be spending on their debit card, in particular for everyday transactions, you need to have some kind of savings buffer around in order to spend on
sentences.zh: 即对于那些想要使用借记卡消费的人，特别是日常交易，你需要有一些储蓄缓冲才能使用

sentences.en: your debit card.
sentences.zh: 你的借记卡。

sentences.en: And so it's actually, it's not the comfort with credit that allows these people to be
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，并不是对信贷的舒适感让这些人

sentences.en: co-holding, but instead, it's almost a discomfort with credit of, right, I want to be more focused
sentences.zh: 进行“共同持有”，相反，这几乎是对信贷的一种不适感，即，我想更专注于

sentences.en: on the fact that I have this money in savings that's available, that can be the driver.
sentences.zh: 基于我储蓄账户里有这笔钱且随时可用这一事实，这可以成为驱动因素。

sentences.en: Again, treating these two pools is like really distinct.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，将这两个资金池视为截然不同的事物。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: So just to wrap up, what are the big questions that you are still trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 那么总结一下，你目前还在试图回答哪些重大问题？

sentences.en: What are you working on right now?
sentences.zh: 你现在正在研究什么？

sentences.en: So great question.
sentences.zh: 问得好。

sentences.en: There are a handful of different topics.
sentences.zh: 有几个不同的课题。

sentences.en: One that I'll mention just because it relates to some of the earlier points that have come up, but is in terms of thinking about buy now, pay later plans and wealth signaling.
sentences.zh: 我提一个，因为它与之前提到的一些观点有关，那就是关于“先买后付”计划和财富信号的问题。

sentences.en: These were sort of two different topics that came up earlier.
sentences.zh: 这在之前是两个不同的话题。

sentences.en: And one of the projects that I've been working on has been looking at what happens when you are using a buy now, pay later plan or any other form of payment method.
sentences.zh: 我正在进行的一个项目，是研究当你使用“先买后付”计划或任何其他支付方式时会发生什么。

sentences.en: What are the kind of wealth signals that people derive from this?
sentences.zh: 人们从中能获取什么样的财富信号？

sentences.en: And so typically, we think about wealth signaling as being really around these highly conspicuous behaviors.
sentences.zh: 通常，我们认为财富信号主要围绕这些高度显眼的消费行为。

sentences.en: So specifically, purchases is sort of the most traditional version of this, right?
sentences.zh: 具体来说，购买商品是最传统的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: I buy a fancy car, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，我买了一辆豪车。

sentences.en: And these are also sort of long lasting transactions, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这些交易通常是持久的，对吧？

sentences.en: Or sort of you have the car and you're displaying it all day long to your friends.
sentences.zh: 或者说，你拥有这辆车，整天都在向朋友展示它。

sentences.en: But what we're proposing in this research is that in addition to the purchases themselves,
sentences.zh: 但我们在研究中提出，除了购买行为本身之外，

sentences.en: that actually the way that you make the purchase can send a wealth signal, both externally,
sentences.zh: 实际上，你进行购买的方式也能发出财富信号，既是对外的，

sentences.en: let's say to the retail, like to the store employee, but also internally, can send a signal of status to yourself as well over how you feel about making the purchase.
sentences.zh: 比如对零售店员，也是对内的，即你对这次购买行为的感受，也能向你自己发出一种地位信号。

sentences.en: And so using the buy now, pay later plan versus a credit card versus a platinum Amex card,
sentences.zh: 因此，使用“先买后付”计划、信用卡或美国运通白金卡，

sentences.en: actually the method of payment can make us feel differently about the expense, which can then have potentially downstream consequences for our likelihood of sort of
sentences.zh: 实际上，支付方式的不同会让我们对这笔开支有不同的感受，这可能会对我们未来

sentences.en: continuing to use these methods and to return to the same stores going forward.
sentences.zh: 继续使用这些支付方式以及再次光顾同一家商店的可能性产生后续影响。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Sussman, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，萨斯曼博士，感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This has been illuminating.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话非常有启发性。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Really fun conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常愉快的谈话。

sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org，或者在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 或任何你收听播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》往期节目。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please follow us and leave a rating.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢我们的内容，请关注我们并留下评分。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future episodes, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的节目有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由李·韦纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯，代表美国心理学会向大家致意。
